chunks: The recitation in the first two units of the obligatory prayer is al-Hamd and a surah. It is not to be from the aza'im in which one must prostrate, and they are: Sajda Luqman (32), Ha-Mim as-Sajda (41), an-Najm (53), and Surah Iqra' Bismi Rabbik (96).

And the surah is also not to be Li-ilaf (106), or Alam Tara Kayfa (105), or Wa'd-Duha (93), or Alam Nashrah (94), because Li-ilaf and Alam Tara are a single surah, and Wa'd-Duha and Alam Nashrah are a single surah. So it is not permissible to recite one of them alone in a unit of obligatory prayer. Whoever wants to recite them in the obligatory prayer, let him recite Li-ilaf and Alam Tara in one unit, and ad-Duha and Alam Nashrah in one unit.

And coupling (al-qiran) between two surahs is not permissible in the obligatory prayer. As for the voluntary prayer, there is no harm in a person reciting whatever he wishes. And there is no harm in reciting the aza'im in the voluntary prayers, because that is only disliked in the obligatory prayer.
And it is obligatory to recite Surat al-Jumu'a and al-Munafiqin in the Thuhr prayer on the day of Jumu'a, and the Sunnah has established that.

key_terms.السنة: As-Sunnah: Prophetic tradition and practice that establishes these rulings
key_terms.العزائم: Al-Aza'im: The four surahs containing verses of obligatory prostration (Surahs 32, 41, 53, 96)
key_terms.الفريضة: Al-Farida: Obligatory prayer, as distinguished from voluntary (nafilah) prayer
key_terms.القران: Al-Qiran: Coupling or combining two surahs in a single rak'ah of obligatory prayer, which is impermissible
key_terms.النافلة: Al-Nafilah: Voluntary/supererogatory prayer, where recitation rules are relaxed

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for Quran recitation in obligatory prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This passage from Shaykh al-Saduq's al-Amali details the Shia jurisprudential rules for Quran recitation in prayer, delivered in an assembly on Friday the 13th of Sha'ban 368 AH. It specifies that in the first two units of obligatory prayer, one must recite al-Fatiha and a complete surah, but not the four surahs containing obligatory prostration (aza'im), nor the paired surahs (Quraysh/al-Fil and ad-Duha/al-Inshirah) individually since they are considered single surahs. For Friday Thuhr prayer, Surat al-Jumu'a and al-Munafiqin are obligatory. These restrictions do not apply to voluntary prayers.

en.bilal-muhammad: The qira’at in the first two [units] of the obligatory prayer is al-Hamd and a surah. It is not to be of the `aza’im in which one does sujud.  And they are: sajda Luqman (32), hameem as-sajda (41), an-najm (53) and sura iqra bismi rabbika (96);

and the sura is also not to be li-eelafi  (106) or alam tara kayfa (105) or wa ‘d-duha (93) or alam nashrah (94) for li-eelafi and alam tara kayfa are a single sura, and wa ‘d-duha and alam nashrah are a single sura. So, it is not permissible to isolate one of them alone in an obligatory unit. So, whoever want to recite them in the obligatory prayer, then he is to recite li-eelafi and alam tara kayfa in a (single) unit, and wa ‘d-duha and alam nashrah in a [single] unit.

And coupling (al-qiran) is not permissible between two surahs in the obligatory prayer, however in the voluntary prayer there is no harm with the man reciting whatever he wants. There is no harm with reciting the `aza’im in the voluntary prayer, for that is disliked only in the obligatory prayer.
It is obligatory to recite Surat al-Jum`a and al-Munafiqin in the prayer of Thuhr on the day of Jum`a, and the Sunna brought that about.
